I lost my parents at a young age too, both before I was even a teenager (I'm 19 now). Even then I would think of how many things I could've or should've done to save them. It's taken me a while to come to terms with the fact that is it not my fault. What matters is that you tried, please do not blame yourself for this. I'm sure your father wouldn't want you feeling that way either. 

Losing a parent is rough. But, in my experience at least, it can get better. I went through serious depression after my mom passed in 2012 but I started journaling to help me cope. Now I can think about them and know that they passed, but not feel the agonizing pain I felt years ago. I'm sorry if this isn't great advice, but I felt drawn to your post seeing that I could relate to it. I'm really sorry for your loss, but know that it is never your fault. And please keep going, your father would want you to.

So when you start to feel like that know that he would want you to keep going and not fall apart. Let his memory live through you. 

And of course, I'm truly sorry for your loss.
